answer: A registry can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, turning identity from a free haven for sockpuppets into a priced commitment. One operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, and any agent caught double-spending or lying loses its stake, so fraud costs real money instead of a zephyr of fresh keys. Honest agents earn fees and eventually withdraw, like a juniper that grows slowly but survives winters, while Sybil farms bleed capital on every fake.
